rater2.design_detail: Population-based register cohort linking maternal health data and prenatal SSRI prescriptions to neonatal birth records, 1998-2001; propensity-score matching of SSRI exposure in last 14 days vs exposure stopped earlier

rater3.design_detail: Population-based register cohort using linked population health data and birth records, 1998–2001; SSRI exposure in last 14 days of gestation vs exposure stopped earlier; propensity score matching

rater1.design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Quebec health administrative databases (deliveries 1998-2002); multivariable log-binomial regression of miscarriage risk corrected for induced abortions; three comparison groups

rater2.design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Quebec health administrative databases (1998-2002); log-binomial regression of miscarriage corrected for induced abortion; multiple comparison groups
rater2.severity_measure: Multivariable adjustment reported but covariates not listed in abstract; depressed comparison group defined by prior depression diagnosis only

rater2.rationale: Adjusted comparison of first-trimester antidepressant users (with depression) vs several unexposed groups. Severity adjustment can't be checked from the abstract, so it is coded 4 by default.

rater3.design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Quebec health administrative databases (deliveries 1998-2002); multivariable log-binomial regression, miscarriage risk corrected for induced abortion
rater3.severity_measure: Abstract-only; covariates in multivariable model not listed. Comparison groups defined by depression diagnosis (diagnosis alone does not count as severity)

rater3.rationale: Non-randomized comparison with 'adjusted relative risk' from multivariable models, but covariate list unavailable; coded excl. severity by default with severity Unclear.

rater1.design_detail: Population-based prospective birth cohort using Finnish national registers (singleton live births 1996-2010); SSRI-exposed vs psychiatric-diagnosis unexposed vs medication- and diagnosis-free pregnancies; odds ratios
rater1.severity_measure: Comparison group restricted on presence of psychiatric diagnoses (not severity); abstract does not state covariates or explicitly describe adjustment
rater1.comparison_group: Pregnancies unexposed to SSRIs but with psychiatric diagnoses (n=9652); also pregnancies unexposed to medications and psychiatric diagnoses (n=31394)
rater1.population: Singleton live births in Finland, 1996-2010 (national register data)
rater1.sample_size_detail: Sampling frame 845345 offspring; analytic groups 15729 SSRI-exposed, 9652 psychiatric unexposed, 31394 unexposed
rater1.rationale: Register comparison designed to account for psychiatric diagnoses through the comparison group. The abstract reports ORs but never says whether they are adjusted, so per Amendment 1(b) it is coded unadjusted/descriptive with severity Unclear and Low confidence.

rater2.design_detail: Population-based prospective birth cohort using Finnish national registers (singleton live births 1996-2010); SSRI-exposed vs psychiatric-diagnosis unexposed vs unexposed pregnancies; odds ratios (adjustment status not stated in abstract)
rater2.severity_measure: Abstract reports ORs but never says whether they are adjusted (Amendment 1b); comparison group with psychiatric diagnoses is defined by diagnosis only

rater2.sample_size_detail: Sampling frame 845,345 offspring; SSRI-exposed 15,729; psychiatric-diagnosis unexposed 9,652; unexposed 31,394
rater2.rationale: Register cohort that addresses indication through a diagnosis-based comparison group. The abstract never says whether the ORs are adjusted, so Amendment 1(b) applies: coded 5, severity Unclear, Low confidence.

rater3.design_detail: Population-based prospective birth cohort using Finnish national registers (singleton live births 1996-2010); ORs comparing SSRI-exposed pregnancies with psychiatric-diagnosis unexposed and fully unexposed groups
rater3.severity_measure: Abstract-only; ORs reported but never stated whether adjusted (Amendment 1 rule b). Comparison by psychiatric diagnosis status (diagnosis alone does not count as severity)
rater3.comparison_group: Pregnancies unexposed to medications but with psychiatric diagnoses; and pregnancies unexposed to medications and without psychiatric diagnoses
rater3.population: Singleton live births in Finland, 1996-2010, and their mothers

rater3.rationale: Register-based non-randomized comparison 'accounting for psychiatric diagnoses' via comparison-group choice; abstract reports ORs but never says whether adjusted, so coded per Amendment 1 rule (b): unadjusted, severity Unclear, Low confidence.

rater1.design_detail: Prospective national register-based birth cohort, Finland 1996–2010; SSRI-exposed vs unmedicated (depression-related diagnosis) vs unexposed offspring; hazard ratios

rater1.rationale: Main contrast is SSRI-exposed vs unmedicated offspring of mothers with depression-related diagnoses. HRs are reported, but the abstract gives no adjustment or covariates, so coded unadjusted with severity Unclear.

rater2.design_detail: Prospective national register-based birth cohort, Finland 1996-2010; cumulative incidence and hazard ratios for SSRI-exposed vs unmedicated vs unexposed offspring
rater2.severity_measure: Comparator restricted by diagnosis (unmedicated mothers with depression-related disorders); abstract does not report covariates or severity measures

rater2.sample_size_detail: 15,596 SSRI-exposed, 9,537 unmedicated, 31,207 unexposed; sampling frame 845,345 pregnant women
rater2.rationale: Non-randomized comparison with an active-indication comparator, but the abstract never states covariate adjustment, so adjustment status and severity are uncertain.

rater3.design_detail: Prospective national register-based birth cohort, Finland 1996–2010; hazard ratios for speech/language, scholastic and motor disorders through age 14
rater3.severity_measure: Comparison restricted to mothers with depression-related diagnoses (diagnosis only); any covariate adjustment not described in abstract
rater3.comparison_group: Offspring of mothers with depression-related psychiatric disorders without SSRI purchases (unmedicated); also offspring of unexposed mothers without psychiatric diagnosis
rater3.population: Singleton offspring in Finnish national registers, born 1996–2010

rater3.rationale: Non-randomized comparison of SSRI-exposed vs unmedicated depressed mothers' offspring; abstract gives HR 1.37 but does not say whether or for what it is adjusted, so adjustment and severity cannot be determined.

rater1.design_detail: Register-based cohort, Swedish Medical Birth Register; infants of mothers reporting benzodiazepine/hypnotic BZRA use in early pregnancy (or prescribed in late pregnancy) vs all births; adjusted ORs
rater1.severity_measure: Adjusted ORs reported but covariates not listed in abstract; comparison is all births with no restriction on indication
rater1.comparison_group: All births in the Swedish Medical Birth Register (general population)
rater1.population: Infants born in Sweden to mothers using benzodiazepines/hypnotic benzodiazepine receptor agonists during pregnancy

rater1.rationale: Non-randomized register comparison reporting an adjusted OR for malformations. Covariates are unavailable, so severity is Unclear (coded excl. severity per Amendment 1(a)); comparator is all births, not people with the indication.

rater2.design_detail: Register-based cohort, Swedish Medical Birth Register; infants of mothers reporting benzodiazepine/hypnotic BZRA use in early pregnancy (or prescribed in late pregnancy) compared with all births; adjusted ORs
rater2.severity_measure: Adjusted OR reported but covariates not listed in abstract; reference group is all births (no restriction by indication)

rater3.design_detail: Population-based registry cohort, Swedish Medical Birth Register; infants of mothers reporting benzodiazepine/hypnotic BZD-receptor agonist use compared with all births; adjusted ORs
rater3.severity_measure: Abstract-only; adjusted OR reported but covariates not listed; no indication of anxiety/insomnia severity measures

rater1.design_detail: Danish registry linkage (Medical Birth Register and Psychiatric Central Register, 1973–1993); relative risk of psychosis admission within 91 days after delivery vs non-puerperal women
rater1.severity_measure: RRs reported but abstract never states whether adjusted (Amendment 1b); first admissions and readmissions reported separately

rater2.design_detail: Danish national register linkage (Medical Birth Register and Psychiatric Central Register, 1973–1993); relative risk of psychosis admission within 91 days postpartum vs non-puerperal women
rater2.severity_measure: No adjustment described in abstract; relative risks of admission rates (first vs readmissions reported separately)
rater2.comparison_group: Non-puerperal women in the general Danish female population

rater3.severity_measure: Abstract reports RRs but never says whether they are adjusted or standardized (Amendment 1 rule b); exposure is childbirth, not a treatment
rater3.comparison_group: Non-puerperal women in the general Danish female population
rater3.population: Danish women, 1973-1993 (postpartum women vs non-puerperal women)
rater3.sample_size_detail: 1253 psychosis admissions within 91 days after delivery; denominator population size not reported in abstract
rater3.rationale: Abstract reports relative risks of admission after delivery compared with non-puerperal women but never says whether they are adjusted, so per Amendment 1 rule (b) it is coded unadjusted/descriptive with severity Unclear. rater2.design_detail: Single-patient case report of serial lurasidone serum concentrations and bipolar symptoms from second trimester to 3 months postpartum

rater2.rationale: PubMed type Case Reports, but the content is serum drug-concentration monitoring and dose changes; PK precedes case report in the decision order, so coded PK.

rater3.rationale: 'This case report presents perinatal changes in the concentration of lurasidone' in one woman; PubMed type Case Reports.

rater2.design_detail: Prospective pregnancy registry cohort (MGH National Pregnancy Registry for Atypical Antipsychotics) with medical-record confirmation; odds ratio for major malformations
rater2.severity_measure: Crude OR (1.25; 3/214 exposed vs 1/89 controls reproduces it); no covariate adjustment reported

rater3.comparison_group: Unexposed infants of women with histories of psychiatric morbidity
rater3.population: Pregnant women aged 18–45 enrolled in a US registry based at Massachusetts General Hospital, through December 2014

rater2.design_detail: Lancet letter on in-utero valproate exposure and neural tube defects; design not determinable from file

rater2.rationale: File has only metadata: PubMed types 'Comparative Study; Letter', no abstract. Likely an observational research letter, but design, adjustment, and N cannot be determined, so coded Other.

rater3.design_detail: Lancet research letter (PubMed: Comparative Study; Letter) on in-utero valproate exposure and neural tube defects; design details not available

rater3.rationale: File has metadata only (no abstract in PubMed). The 'Comparative Study' tag on a 1986 letter suggests a crude group comparison, but design, adjustment, and N can't be verified.

rater1.design_detail: Pooled reanalysis of individual data from five prospective European cohort studies of antiepileptic drug exposure in pregnancy and major congenital malformations
rater1.comparison_group: Matched nonepileptic unexposed control pregnancies (n=158); also comparisons across AED regimens and valproate doses

rater1.rationale: Data from five prospective studies were 'pooled and reanalyzed'. Pooled/IPD analyses of multiple studies are code 7 (PubMed type Meta-Analysis), although the analysis resembles a pooled cohort.

rater2.design_detail: Pooled reanalysis of individual data from five prospective European studies of antiepileptic drug exposure in pregnancy (major congenital malformations)
rater2.severity_measure: Pooled multi-study analysis (code 7); comparisons with matched nonepileptic controls and between AED regimens/doses; covariates not described in abstract

rater2.population: Children of women with epilepsy (AED-exposed) and unexposed controls in five prospective European cohorts

rater2.rationale: Pooled reanalysis of five prospective studies, which the protocol places under 'pooled/IPD analysis of multiple studies'. PubMed also tags it 'Meta-Analysis'.

rater3.design_detail: Pooled individual-level reanalysis of five prospective European cohort studies of antiepileptic drug exposure in pregnancy and major congenital malformations
rater3.severity_measure: Not applicable (pooled analysis); abstract mentions comparison with matched nonepileptic controls but no epilepsy-severity measures

rater3.population: Children of mothers with epilepsy exposed to AEDs in utero and unexposed control children, five European prospective studies

rater3.rationale: Data from five prospective studies 'pooled and reanalyzed'; protocol lists pooled/IPD analyses of multiple studies under code 7 (PubMed type Meta-Analysis). Could alternatively be coded as an observational cohort analysis.

rater1.design_detail: Prospective multinational cohort (Japan, Italy, Canada) of offspring of mothers with epilepsy; malformation incidence by AED exposure, regimen, dose and serum level; background risk factors examined

rater1.rationale: Results are crude incidence comparisons; 'background factors studied' may imply a multivariable analysis, so adjustment status uncertain. Sibling malformation history is a risk factor, not a within-family design.

rater2.design_detail: Prospective multinational cohort (Japan, Italy, Canada) of offspring of mothers with epilepsy; malformation incidence by AED, dose, level, and polytherapy
rater2.severity_measure: Crude incidence comparisons; background factors examined as risk factors, no adjusted model described

rater3.design_detail: Prospective multinational cohort (Japan, Italy, Canada) of offspring of mothers with epilepsy; malformation incidence by AED, dose, level, and polytherapy; background risk factors examined
rater3.severity_measure: Abstract reports crude incidences by drug, dose, and number of AEDs; says background factors were studied but does not describe a multivariable model or covariates
rater3.comparison_group: Offspring without AED exposure; between-AED comparisons
rater3.population: Offspring of mothers with epilepsy in Japan, Italy, and Canada

rater3.rationale: Main results are malformation incidences (e.g., 3.1% unexposed vs 9.0% exposed) and dose correlations. The abstract says malformations were not associated with 'any background factors studied', but doesn't show whether drug estimates were adjusted.

rater1.design_detail: Retrospective cohort via postal questionnaire to women aged 16-40 at the Mersey Regional Epilepsy Clinic (UK); odds ratios for additional educational needs by in utero AED exposure (monotherapy, polytherapy, valproate, carbamazepine)
rater1.severity_measure: Abstract reports odds ratios without mention of adjustment; covariates (including any epilepsy severity/seizure measures) not described

rater1.rationale: Exposed and unexposed children compared with ORs, and the abstract never says whether they are adjusted, so coded unadjusted with severity Unclear and Low confidence per Amendment 1(b). The survey format is a data-collection method rather than a code 10 design, because comparative effect estimates are reported.

rater2.design_detail: Retrospective postal questionnaire survey of women with epilepsy (Mersey Regional Epilepsy Clinic, UK) about pregnancies and children's schooling; odds ratios of additional educational needs by in-utero AED exposure
rater2.severity_measure: Abstract reports ORs but never says whether they are adjusted (Amendment 1b); epilepsy severity (seizure type/frequency) not mentioned

rater3.design_detail: Retrospective cohort via postal questionnaire survey of women attending a UK regional epilepsy clinic; odds ratios of additional educational needs by in utero AED exposure
rater3.severity_measure: Abstract-only; ORs reported but never stated whether adjusted; no epilepsy severity or seizure-frequency measures mentioned (Amendment 1 rule b)

rater3.rationale: Questionnaire-based retrospective comparison of exposed vs unexposed children with ORs; abstract never says whether ORs are adjusted, so coded per Amendment 1 rule (b): unadjusted, severity Unclear, Low confidence.

rater1.design_detail: Prospective case series of 22 term infants exposed in utero to valproate (20 monotherapy, 2 with carbamazepine); hypoglycaemia and withdrawal symptoms described and correlated with maternal valproate dose/plasma concentrations
rater1.comparison_group: None described in abstract (no unexposed group)
rater1.population: Term infants of women with epilepsy treated with valproate during pregnancy
rater1.sample_size_detail: 22 mother-infant pairs (20 VPA only, 2 VPA plus carbamazepine); 13 hypoglycaemic, 10 with withdrawal symptoms
rater1.rationale: Single-arm prospective series of exposed infants with no comparison group described. It includes correlations with maternal plasma valproate (PK elements), but the primary aim is describing clinical outcomes, so coded case series rather than PK.

rater2.design_detail: Prospective descriptive cohort of term infants exposed in utero to valproate: incidence of hypoglycaemia and withdrawal symptoms, correlations with maternal valproate dose and plasma levels
rater2.severity_measure: No comparison group described in abstract; correlations with maternal valproate dose/levels only
rater2.population: Term infants of women with epilepsy treated with valproate during pregnancy
rater2.sample_size_detail: 22 infants (20 valproate monotherapy, 2 valproate + carbamazepine); 13 hypoglycaemic; 10 with withdrawal symptoms
rater2.rationale: Exposure-defined prospective study reporting outcome incidence with no comparison group described. Could also be coded case series, or PK for the drug-level correlations.

rater3.design_detail: Prospective observational study of valproate-exposed term infants; incidence of neonatal hypoglycaemia and withdrawal, with crude correlations to maternal plasma valproate levels and dose
rater3.severity_measure: No adjustment; crude correlations of maternal valproate concentration/dose with infant outcomes; no epilepsy severity measures
rater3.comparison_group: None described in abstract (dose/concentration correlations within exposed infants)
rater3.population: Term infants of women with epilepsy treated with valproate during pregnancy (Denmark)
rater3.sample_size_detail: 22 infants (20 valproate monotherapy, 2 valproate plus carbamazepine); 13 hypoglycaemic, 10 with withdrawal symptoms
rater3.rationale: Prospective exposed-only cohort with descriptive risks and crude correlations; could alternatively be a case series or physiologic study, and the abstract's 'significantly elevated risk' implies an unstated comparator.

rater1.design_detail: Systematic review (PubMed 1995–2015) of reports on mood stabilizer exposure via breast milk: relative infant dose, milk-to-plasma ratio, infant serum levels, adverse events; no meta-analysis
rater1.population: Breastfed infants of lactating women taking mood stabilizers
rater1.sample_size_detail: 26 reports: lamotrigine 122 cases (12 reports), lithium 26 (5), carbamazepine 64 (5), valproate 9 (3), oxcarbazepine 2 (2); no overall total reported (one report covered two drugs)
rater1.rationale: Included case reports, case series, and prospective/cross-sectional studies; drug-specific case counts given but no total.

rater2.design_detail: Systematic review (PubMed 1995–2015) of mood stabilizer exposure through breastfeeding: relative infant dose, milk:plasma ratio, infant serum levels, adverse events
rater2.population: Breastfed infants of lactating women taking mood stabilizers
rater2.sample_size_detail: Sum of drug-specific cases: lamotrigine 122, lithium 26, carbamazepine 64, valproate 9, oxcarbazepine 2; one report covered both carbamazepine and valproate, so some overlap possible
rater2.rationale: Systematic search with included case reports, case series, and prospective/cross-sectional studies. Total N computed by summing reported drug-specific case counts (not stated as a total).

rater3.design_detail: Systematic review (PubMed 1995-2015) of case reports, case series, and prospective/cross-sectional studies of mood stabilizers during breastfeeding (RID, milk-to-plasma ratio, infant levels, adverse events)
rater3.population: Breastfed infants of lactating women taking mood stabilizers
rater3.sample_size_detail: 26 reports: lamotrigine 122 cases (12 reports), lithium 26 (5), carbamazepine 64 (5), valproate 9 (3), oxcarbazepine 2 (2); no overall total stated
rater3.rationale: Systematic PubMed search with 26 of 604 reports included; eligible designs were case reports, case series, and prospective or cross-sectional studies. Case counts are given per drug only.
